criterion_scores.reasoning: The high-level behavior matches the intended two-stage scanner: Stage A avoids `get_thread`, Stage B is allowlist-only, the distill subagent has no write tools, HITL gates precede writes, and the skill routes through the guarded spine path. However, correctness has load-bearing internal contradictions in the URL/dedup/write path: `canonical_url` vs `primary_url` naming diverges (lines 117, 129, 164), B5 reintroduces coarse title/date/kind dedup despite the canonical-URL invariant (lines 135, 139, 164), and B5 loses merged newsletter provenance by writing `sources:["inbox"]` instead of all citing sources (lines 139, 164). The Stage A treatment of Gmail snippets as metadata is also a safety-boundary ambiguity. This is at the pass line but needs review before relying on the skill operationally.

The artifact contains the main required parts for a skill: inputs, Stage A discovery, Stage B extraction, HITL gates, write steps, failure modes, confidence/gaps, and references. The supplied deterministic reference check reports no missing `.claude` references. Completeness is reduced because two operational dependencies are under-specified: the processed-message-id ledger fallback has no path/schema/update procedure (line 178), and the alias table is a load-bearing resolution input but has an ambiguous path and sparse growth protocol (line 133). These are not TODO stubs, but they leave obvious failure paths thin.

Project skill naming/frontmatter are correct (`name: inbox-miner`, no `alex:` prefix), placement is consistent with `.claude/skills/`, and the artifact observes key house constraints: subagent extraction is text-in/structured-out with no write tools (lines 22, 99), MCP Notion writes are parent-thread only (line 167), Supabase is used as the sanctioned Market-Intelligence store rather than a measurement store, and line 221-228 explicitly routes writes through `spine_client`/`spine_write.py`. Minor convention risk remains around the ambiguous alias-map path and duplicated live Gmail label IDs, but the main conventions are followed.

The design is mostly contract-first and safety-oriented rather than platform-building: it uses allowlists, boundary filters, HITL gates, canonical URL dedup, and guarded writes. It does not resurrect the tombstoned decisions listed in the prompt and does not hardcode secrets. The main nit is duplicated mutable state: live Gmail label IDs are embedded even though the skill warns to re-resolve them (lines 214-216). The artifact is long, but most detail is operationally justified by the privacy/write-safety risks rather than generic ceremony.

Diagnostics are generally strong: failure modes are explicit (lines 176-183), coverage reporting is required rather than overclaimed (line 50), `SUPABASE_API_KEY` absence hard-fails loudly (line 160), label mechanics include read-back warnings (lines 206-219), and the confidence/gaps section is candid (lines 185-189). The main diagnostic weakness is that some load-bearing names and fallbacks are ambiguous enough to make failures harder to interpret (`canonical_url`/`primary_url`, and the unspecified processed ledger), but the artifact is otherwise legible and honest about boundaries.

defects.location: Stage A / A1 — Pull sender metadata
defects.spec_ref: Artifact Stage A metadata-only/no-body invariant, lines 37-39 and line 48
defects.description: The skill treats Gmail `snippet` as metadata during the discovery pass, but snippets are body previews and can contain private content. Line 48 then says the boundary filter retains metadata only and never snippet/body, so the instructions are internally ambiguous about whether Stage A may ingest or pass snippets.

defects.quote: `primary_url` MUST be the canonical primary source — redirect-resolution is MANDATORY (not optional).
defects.location: Stage B / B2 — Structured extraction URL field
defects.spec_ref: Artifact extraction schema, line 117; write payload, line 164
defects.description: The extraction schema defines `canonical_url` as the required dedup/source field, but this section switches to `primary_url`, and B5 writes `url:primary_url`. That field-name split is load-bearing: an implementer could validate one field and write another, breaking source resolution and dedup.

defects.quote: Dedup on (title, event_date::date, kind) as a backstop.
defects.location: Stage B / B5 — Insert the signal event
defects.spec_ref: Artifact canonical-URL dedup invariant, lines 135 and 139
defects.description: Earlier sections say the resolved canonical URL is the primary dedup key and warn that `(company, kind, date)` falsely merges same-company same-day events. B5 still instructs dedup on a coarse title/date/kind tuple; because the title is only `"{company} — {kind}"`, this can reproduce the exact false-merge mode the skill says is load-bearing to avoid.

defects.location: Stage B / B5 — Insert the signal event metadata
defects.spec_ref: Artifact run-batched cross-newsletter dedup requirement, lines 137-139
defects.description: B3.5 requires a merged event row to carry all citing newsletters in `metadata.sources` plus `source_count`. The write payload instead collapses provenance to a generic `sources:["inbox"]`, losing the cross-newsletter evidence the gate and dedup logic depend on.

defects.quote: fall back to a self-maintained processed-message-id ledger for idempotency, and a manual worksheet for noise.
defects.location: Failure modes — Gmail label-write / spam-write scope not granted
defects.description: The fallback ledger is load-bearing for idempotency if Gmail label writes fail, but the skill never gives its path, schema, update point, or read-back procedure. The normal processed-label path is detailed, but the advertised fallback is under-specified.

defects.quote: Seed the alias table in `inbox-miner/references/aliases.md`; it grows per run like `signal-taxonomy.md`.
defects.description: The alias map is part of deterministic entity resolution, but its path is ambiguous relative to the skill directory and it is not listed in the Reuses/references section. The skill also does not specify the review/write convention for growing it, unlike the clearer treatment of `signal-taxonomy.md`.

defects.location: Gmail label mechanics — Live Pipeline taxonomy
defects.description: Embedding environment-specific Gmail label IDs in the skill duplicates mutable external state. Line 216 correctly says to re-resolve and never hardcode, so this is mitigated, but the live IDs are still stale-state surface that can mislead future runs.

checks_performed: Checked skill frontmatter/name placement against project-skill conventions, including absence of an alex: prefix.
Checked Stage A/Stage B safety boundary: metadata-only discovery, allowlist-only body reads, denylist/boundary filter, HITL gates, and no subagent writes.

Checked write path instructions against the artifact’s own invariants: schema-validated extraction, canonical URL requirement, dedup order, single guarded spine write path, Notion parent-thread writes, and label-after-write idempotency.
Checked failure modes and honest-gap sections for concrete fallback instructions and overclaims.
Checked references/tombstones against the supplied deterministic checks: no verified-missing .claude references and no live removed-tool hits.
Checked for anti-patterns called out by the rubric: tombstoned stack decisions, hardcoded secrets, fabricated specificity, duplicated state, speculative surface, and bypassing guarded writes.
